tz_key_cards.name: Blood Artist
tz_key_cards.why: Whenever any creature dies, including theirs, the player you target loses 1 life and you gain 1. The defining card of the archetype.

tz_key_cards.name: Zulaport Cutthroat
tz_key_cards.why: Counts only your own creatures, but drains each opponent instead of one target. Redundancy is what turns a cute engine into a consistent kill.

tz_key_cards.name: Bastion of Remembrance
tz_key_cards.why: A third copy on an enchantment, which is much harder for most decks to remove than a 0/1 body.

tz_key_cards.name: Viscera Seer
tz_key_cards.why: A free sacrifice outlet on a one-drop, with scry attached. Being free and repeatable matters far more than the scry.

tz_key_cards.name: Ashnod's Altar
tz_key_cards.why: Sacrifice for two colorless mana. The outlet that most combo lines in the archetype are built around.

tz_key_cards.name: Phyrexian Altar
tz_key_cards.why: The same at one mana of any color, which fixes as well as ramps and enables far more loops.

tz_key_cards.name: Goblin Bombardment
tz_key_cards.why: A free outlet that deals a damage each time, so it is an outlet and a win condition in one two-mana enchantment.

tz_key_cards.name: Pitiless Plunderer
tz_key_cards.why: A Treasure for every creature that dies, which pays for the next sacrifice and turns many loops infinite.

tz_key_cards.name: Grave Pact
tz_key_cards.why: Every creature you lose costs each opponent one too. Turns your engine into a one-sided board wipe on repeat.

tz_key_cards.name: Dictate of Erebos
tz_key_cards.why: The same effect with flash, so it lands after a wrath or in response to removal on your commander.

tz_key_commanders.name: Teysa Karlov
tz_key_commanders.why: Doubles every death trigger and gives your tokens vigilance and lifelink. The most direct payoff commander in the archetype.

tz_key_commanders.name: Korvold, Fae-Cursed King
tz_key_commanders.why: Draws and grows on every sacrifice, of any permanent type. The best card-advantage engine of any aristocrats commander.

tz_key_commanders.name: Yawgmoth, Thran Physician
tz_key_commanders.why: A free outlet, a draw engine, and repeatable removal on one four-drop. Rewrites what the deck is allowed to do.

tz_key_commanders.name: Judith, the Scourge Diva
tz_key_commanders.why: Anthem plus a damage per nontoken death, aiming the engine at creatures as well as at players.

tz_key_commanders.name: Ayara, First of Locthwain
tz_key_commanders.why: Drains on every black creature entering and converts creatures into cards. Mono-black and relentlessly consistent.

tz_key_commanders.name: Marchesa, the Black Rose
tz_key_commanders.why: Returns your creatures when they die with a counter on them, which makes sacrificing genuinely free.

tz_key_commanders.name: Shirei, Shizo's Caretaker
tz_key_commanders.why: Returns every one-power creature that died this turn, every turn. A recursion engine built for sacrifice loops.

tz_key_commanders.name: Chatterfang, Squirrel General
tz_key_commanders.why: Adds a Squirrel to every token you make and turns the board into removal. Fuel supply and outlet in one.

tz_key_commanders.name: Juri, Master of the Revue
tz_key_commanders.why: Grows on every sacrifice and dumps all that damage at a player when he dies. A sacrifice deck with a built-in finisher.

tz_key_commanders.name: Braids, Arisen Nightmare
tz_key_commanders.why: Turns your own sacrifices into cards or life loss and makes opponents choose which. Value even when the engine stalls.

aristocrats.tz_watch_out: Aristocrats decks can drain the table from a board that looks harmless, which is why experienced pods kill a Blood Artist on sight. Run enough redundancy that losing one payoff is not losing the game, and be honest at Rule 0. A deck that wins from an empty-looking board without attacking surprises people, and the surprise is the part that causes friction.

tz_key_cards.name: Doubling Season
tz_key_cards.why: Doubles tokens and counters. Expensive, format-defining, and the single most impactful card the archetype can draw.

tz_key_cards.name: Anointed Procession
tz_key_cards.why: The white half of the effect at four mana, and the reason token decks run several doublers rather than one.

tz_key_cards.name: Parallel Lives
tz_key_cards.why: The green half. Stacking two doublers quadruples output, which is how a modest token engine becomes a lethal one in a turn.

tz_key_cards.name: Cathars' Crusade
tz_key_cards.why: A plus-one-plus-one counter on everything for every creature that enters. Grows the whole board geometrically and ends games quickly.

tz_key_cards.name: Divine Visitation
tz_key_cards.why: Every token becomes a 4/4 Angel with flying and vigilance instead. Turns quantity directly into quality.

tz_key_cards.name: Craterhoof Behemoth
tz_key_cards.why: Mass pump and trample on a haste body. The archetype's most reliable one-card kill from a developed board.

tz_key_cards.name: Intangible Virtue
tz_key_cards.why: Two mana for a token-only anthem plus vigilance, which is exactly the rate a deck that makes twelve of them wants.

tz_key_cards.name: Skullclamp
tz_key_cards.why: Equip a 1/1, it dies, draw two. Converts surplus tokens into a card-draw engine and fixes the archetype's biggest weakness.

tz_key_cards.name: Impact Tremors
tz_key_cards.why: A damage to each opponent per creature entering. Wins without combat, which matters against decks full of blockers.

tz_key_cards.name: Secure the Wastes
tz_key_cards.why: An instant-speed X tokens, so it dodges sorcery-speed wraths and can be held until the turn it is lethal.

tz_key_commanders.name: Krenko, Mob Boss
tz_key_commanders.why: Doubles your goblin count on every tap. The fastest token accumulation in the format if it survives a rotation.

tz_key_commanders.name: Adeline, Resplendent Cathar
tz_key_commanders.why: A Human token per opponent on every attack, and she grows with the board. Aggro and go-wide in the same card.

tz_key_commanders.name: Rhys the Redeemed
tz_key_commanders.why: A one-drop that first makes tokens and then copies your entire board. The cleanest scaling in the archetype.

tz_key_commanders.name: Trostani, Selesnya's Voice
tz_key_commanders.why: Populate plus lifegain on every creature entering, which buys the turns a wide board needs to set up.

tz_key_commanders.name: Ghave, Guru of Spores
tz_key_commanders.why: Converts counters into tokens and back. The bridge between go-wide, counters, and aristocrats, and a combo engine besides.

tz_key_commanders.name: Jetmir, Nexus of Revels
tz_key_commanders.why: Escalating buffs at three, six, and nine attackers. A commander that states the archetype's thresholds as text.

tz_key_commanders.name: Prossh, Skyraider of Kher
tz_key_commanders.why: Kobolds scaling with the commander tax you have already paid, and a built-in sacrifice outlet.

tz_key_commanders.name: The Locust God
tz_key_commanders.why: A hasty flier per card drawn. The blue exception, powered by draw spells rather than by anthems.

tz_key_commanders.name: Purphoros, God of the Forge
tz_key_commanders.why: Two damage per creature entering, from an indestructible non-creature body. Wins through blockers and through wraths.

tz_key_commanders.name: Emmara, Soul of the Accord
tz_key_commanders.why: A token whenever she taps, including for convoke, so she produces every turn without ever attacking.

tokens.tz_watch_out: One board wipe undoes an hour of work, and go-wide is the archetype wraths are printed to punish. Hold something back, run protection like Heroic Intervention or Boros Charm, and resist the urge to dump your whole hand before you can actually win. The second failure mode is quieter: a wide board with no finisher just sits there, so make sure the deck can convert numbers into damage.

tribal.plan: density of one creature type; lords stack multiplicatively; payoffs reward casting or attacking with the type
stages: early: type two-drops and cost reducers
finish: mass pump or type-specific payoff
wins: mass pump on a wide board
tribal.weak: board wipes, Engineered Plague, Extinction; targeted removal on lords; filler creatures kept only for type
tribal.notes: Concordia rule H74: tribe match counts only with tribal abilities. Tag niche:tribal marks cards that only pay off in a matching deck.

tz_key_cards.name: Cavern of Souls
tz_key_cards.why: A land that makes your chosen type uncounterable. Expensive, but no other card protects a tribal deck's key spells this cleanly.

tz_key_cards.name: Path of Ancestry
tz_key_cards.why: The budget-friendly version of the same idea, adding a scry whenever it pays for a creature of your type.

tz_key_cards.name: Vanquisher's Banner
tz_key_cards.why: An anthem that also draws a card for every creature of your type you cast. Fixes the archetype's card-advantage problem.

tz_key_cards.name: Herald's Horn
tz_key_cards.why: Cost reduction plus a free card off the top each upkeep when it hits your type. Cheap and consistently excellent.

tz_key_cards.name: Kindred Discovery
tz_key_cards.why: Draws whenever a creature of your type enters or attacks. The most explosive draw engine available to any tribe.

tz_key_cards.name: Coat of Arms
tz_key_cards.why: Every creature gets plus-one-plus-one for each other creature sharing a type. Enormous, and symmetrical enough to be dangerous.

tz_key_cards.name: Shared Animosity
tz_key_cards.why: The one-sided version for attackers only, which usually converts a developed board into lethal on the spot.

tz_key_cards.name: Metallic Mimic
tz_key_cards.why: A two-drop that names your type and puts a counter on every one that follows. Works in any color.

tz_key_cards.name: Urza's Incubator
tz_key_cards.why: Two generic mana off every creature spell of your type. The single biggest cost reduction available to tribal decks.

tz_key_cards.name: Patriarch's Bidding
tz_key_cards.why: Returns every creature of the named types from all graveyards. The archetype's post-wrath reset button.

tz_key_commanders.name: Edgar Markov
tz_key_commanders.why: Vampires. Makes a token from the command zone on every Vampire cast, which is unmatched value for a tribal commander.

tz_key_commanders.name: The Ur-Dragon
tz_key_commanders.why: Dragons. Cost reduction on Dragons and a free permanent from hand on every Dragon that connects.

tz_key_commanders.name: Sliver Overlord
tz_key_commanders.why: Slivers. Tutors any Sliver repeatedly, which makes the deck the most consistent tribal build in the format.

tz_key_commanders.name: Lathril, Blade of the Elves
tz_key_commanders.why: Elves. Makes tokens on damage and converts a wide Elf board into a drain that ignores blockers entirely.

tz_key_commanders.name: Wilhelt, the Rotcleaver
tz_key_commanders.why: Zombies. Turns every Zombie death into a Decayed token and a card, which is the whole aristocrats overlap in one commander.

tz_key_commanders.name: Kumena, Tyrant of Orazca
tz_key_commanders.why: Merfolk. Three abilities that convert a Merfolk board into unblockable damage, cards, and counters.

tz_key_commanders.name: Gishath, Sun's Avatar
tz_key_commanders.why: Dinosaurs. Puts Dinosaurs directly from library to battlefield on combat damage, and a single hit often ends the game.

tz_key_commanders.name: Najeela, the Blade-Blossom
tz_key_commanders.why: Warriors. Tokens on attack, and with five colors available she takes infinite combat steps.

tz_key_commanders.name: Muxus, Goblin Grandee
tz_key_commanders.why: Goblins. Digs six deep and puts every Goblin found onto the battlefield at once.

tz_key_commanders.name: Kaalia of the Vast
tz_key_commanders.why: Angels, Demons, and Dragons. Cheats one onto the battlefield attacking, every combat, from turn four.

tribal.tz_watch_out: Tribal decks lose to board wipes harder than anything except go-wide, and the lords make targeted removal unusually effective too. Build in recursion (Patriarch's Bidding is in the archetype's top ten for a reason) and resist filling the last ten slots with weak creatures purely because they share a type. A bad card is still a bad card when it is on-theme.

voltron.plan: one protected threat (usually the commander) wins by 21 commander damage, often in two swings
stages: hold protection so removal or bounce does not reset
remove players one at a time
voltron.weak: edicts, exile, mass bounce bypass protection; Maze of Ith, fog, propaganda; commander tax; aura-heavy builds lose cards when the creature dies

tz_key_cards.name: Lightning Greaves
tz_key_cards.why: Zero-cost equip granting haste and shroud. The most-played protection equipment in the format, and often the first thing a Voltron deck finds.

tz_key_cards.name: Swiftfoot Boots
tz_key_cards.why: Hexproof instead of shroud, so you can still target your own creature with auras. The two boots do different jobs and most decks run both.

tz_key_cards.name: Shadowspear
tz_key_cards.why: Trample and lifelink for one mana, plus the ability to strip hexproof and indestructible from blockers. Small, cheap, and always relevant.

tz_key_cards.name: Sword of Feast and Famine
tz_key_cards.why: Protection from two colors, an opponent discards, and your lands untap. The best of the sword cycle for a deck that wants to keep casting after combat.

tz_key_cards.name: Colossus Hammer
tz_key_cards.why: Plus ten, minus ten, with an eight-mana equip cost that decks solve with Sigarda's Aid or equipment-cost reduction. A one-card kill when it works.

tz_key_cards.name: Whispersilk Cloak
tz_key_cards.why: Unblockable and shroud in one card. Evasion and protection stapled together is exactly what the archetype is short on.

tz_key_cards.name: Rancor
tz_key_cards.why: Two power, trample, and it comes back to hand when it goes to the graveyard. Auras are card disadvantage; Rancor simply is not.

tz_key_cards.name: Ethereal Armor
tz_key_cards.why: Scales with your enchantment count and grants first strike, which is why aura-based Voltron builds get better the longer they go.

tz_key_cards.name: Bear Umbra
tz_key_cards.why: Untaps your lands on attack and shields the creature from the next removal spell via totem armor. Protection and ramp on one aura.

tz_key_cards.name: Kaldra Compleat
tz_key_cards.why: A free 5/5 germ with first strike, trample, haste, and indestructible, and it exiles whatever it damages. A whole Voltron package in one card.

tz_key_commanders.name: Uril, the Miststalker
tz_key_commanders.why: Untargetable by opponents and grows with every aura you attach. The most protected Voltron commander in the format.

tz_key_commanders.name: Rafiq of the Many
tz_key_commanders.why: Exalted plus double strike means a single attacker converts every pump effect into twice the damage.

tz_key_commanders.name: Bruna, Light of Alabaster
tz_key_commanders.why: Attaches every aura from your hand and graveyard on attack, rebuilding the whole stack after a removal spell.

tz_key_commanders.name: Sram, Senior Edificer
tz_key_commanders.why: Draws on every equipment, aura, or vehicle. Mono-white, cheap, and solves the archetype's card-advantage problem outright.

tz_key_commanders.name: Halvar, God of Battle
tz_key_commanders.why: Moves equipment and auras around at no cost, and flips into an equipment that returns the creature it kills.

tz_key_commanders.name: Light-Paws, Emperor's Voice
tz_key_commanders.why: Tutors an aura onto the battlefield with each aura you cast, chaining a whole suite out of a single card.

tz_key_commanders.name: Syr Gwyn, Hero of Ashvale
tz_key_commanders.why: Free equip costs for Knights plus card draw on damage. A Voltron commander that can spread across a team.

tz_key_commanders.name: Nazahn, Revered Bladesmith
tz_key_commanders.why: Tutors an equipment on entry and gives your equipped creatures trample. Consistency plus evasion in the command zone.

tz_key_commanders.name: Skullbriar, the Walking Grave
tz_key_commanders.why: Keeps its counters when it changes zones, so removal costs you a turn rather than the whole investment.

tz_key_commanders.name: Greven, Predator Captain
tz_key_commanders.why: Draws cards equal to the life you paid and grows accordingly. The black Voltron shell, powered by its own life total.

voltron.tz_watch_out: Everything is in one card, and Swords to Plowshares costs one mana. Assume your commander will eat removal three or four times a game and build for it: cheap protection, recursion for your equipment, and a realistic sense of how much tax you can pay. Also watch the table read: a growing Voltron threat is visible to everyone, so you will be attacked before you are ready more often than any other archetype.

tz_key_cards.name: Reanimate
tz_key_cards.why: One black mana for any creature in any graveyard. The most efficient reanimation spell ever printed, and the life loss rarely matters at 40.

tz_key_cards.name: Animate Dead
tz_key_cards.why: Two mana, sticks around as an enchantment, and hits any graveyard. The redundancy that makes the plan consistent.

tz_key_cards.name: Entomb
tz_key_cards.why: One mana to put exactly the card you want into your own graveyard. Turns a reanimation spell into a tutor for anything.

tz_key_cards.name: Buried Alive
tz_key_cards.why: Three creatures into the yard at once, which sets up both a reanimation spell and a mass-return effect in a single card.

tz_key_cards.name: Living Death
tz_key_cards.why: Everyone's graveyard creatures swap with the battlefield. In a deck built for it this is a one-sided board wipe that also rebuilds your team.

tz_key_cards.name: Eternal Witness
tz_key_cards.why: Returns any card from your graveyard on a body that can itself be recurred. The archetype's most-copied effect for a reason.

tz_key_cards.name: Victimize
tz_key_cards.why: Sacrifice one creature, return two tapped. Converts a spare token into your two best creatures at instant-speed value.

tz_key_cards.name: Persist
tz_key_cards.why: Two mana reanimation with a real drawback (the creature comes back with a minus-one-minus-one counter) that costs you almost nothing on a large body.

tz_key_cards.name: Sun Titan
tz_key_cards.why: Recurs a permanent worth three or less on every attack. The white grind engine that keeps rebuilding after a wrath.

tz_key_cards.name: Necromancy
tz_key_cards.why: Animate Dead with an instant-speed flash mode, which lets you reanimate in response to removal or at the end of an opponent's turn.

tz_key_commanders.name: Meren of Clan Nel Toth
tz_key_commanders.why: Free recursion every end step, scaling with experience counters. The definitive value-recursion commander.

tz_key_commanders.name: Muldrotha, the Gravetide
tz_key_commanders.why: One permanent of each type per turn from the graveyard. Turns lands, artifacts, and enchantments into recursion targets, not just creatures.

tz_key_commanders.name: Karador, Ghost Chieftain
tz_key_commanders.why: Costs less the fuller your graveyard is, and casts a creature from it every turn. Built to be milled.

tz_key_commanders.name: Alesha, Who Smiles at Death
tz_key_commanders.why: Reanimates a small creature on attack, for free, at a mana value cap that hides an enormous number of powerful bodies.

tz_key_commanders.name: Chainer, Nightmare Adept
tz_key_commanders.why: Discard a card to cast a creature from your graveyard with haste: the fill and the payoff in one activated ability.

tz_key_commanders.name: Sheoldred, Whispering One
tz_key_commanders.why: Returns a creature to you and forces a sacrifice from everyone else each turn. A commander that attacks the archetype from both sides.

tz_key_commanders.name: The Mimeoplasm
tz_key_commanders.why: Exiles two creatures from graveyards and becomes a hybrid of them. Rewards milling the whole table, not just yourself.

tz_key_commanders.name: Gisa and Geralf
tz_key_commanders.why: Self-mill on cast plus one graveyard Zombie per turn, the natural bridge between recursion and tribal.

tz_key_commanders.name: Sedris, the Traitor King
tz_key_commanders.why: Grants unearth to everything in your graveyard, so any creature you mill becomes a hasty one-shot attacker.

tz_key_commanders.name: Varina, Lich Queen
tz_key_commanders.why: Draw-and-discard on attack, which fills the yard while it builds the board. Fill and payoff on the same trigger.

graveyard.tz_watch_out: Graveyard hate is the most commonly played sideboard-style effect in Commander, and a single Rest in Peace can turn the deck off entirely. Build in a way that survives it: keep some number of cards that are fine cast from hand, run answers to enchantments and artifacts, and avoid a line where every win requires the graveyard to be intact.

cash graveyards for recursion, theft or drain
wins: empty libraries with doubled mill or Traumatize
self-mill into Jace, Wielder of Mysteries / Laboratory Maniac

tz_key_cards.name: Glimpse the Unthinkable
tz_key_cards.why: Ten cards for two mana at sorcery speed. Still the most efficient single-target mill spell in the format.

tz_key_cards.name: Maddening Cacophony
tz_key_cards.why: Eight to one player, or with kicker a quarter of every opponent's library at once. Built for multiplayer in a way most mill cards are not.

tz_key_cards.name: Fractured Sanity
tz_key_cards.why: Fourteen cards for three mana, with cycling so it is never a dead draw. The efficiency ceiling for single-target mill.

tz_key_cards.name: Traumatize
tz_key_cards.why: Halves a library in one card. Enormous on turn five, notably worse later. Mill's timing is the opposite of most decks'.

tz_key_cards.name: Hedron Crab
tz_key_cards.why: Three cards off every land drop, including on other players' turns with a fetchland. A one-drop that accumulates absurd totals.

tz_key_cards.name: Ruin Crab
tz_key_cards.why: The functional reprint, and the reason a mill deck can run eight crabs. Redundancy matters more here than raw power.

tz_key_cards.name: Psychic Corrosion
tz_key_cards.why: Mills every opponent whenever you draw, which turns a normal blue draw engine into a table-wide clock.

tz_key_cards.name: Sphinx's Tutelage
tz_key_cards.why: The same effect aimed at one opponent, with a repeat clause on matching colors that makes it wildly variable and occasionally lethal.

tz_key_cards.name: Altar of Dementia
tz_key_cards.why: A free sacrifice outlet that mills for the sacrificed creature's power. The bridge between mill and any token or aristocrats shell.

tz_key_cards.name: Mesmeric Orb
tz_key_cards.why: Mills everyone for every untap, including yours. Symmetrical, but you are the only player at the table who wants it.

tz_key_commanders.name: Bruvac the Grandiloquent
tz_key_commanders.why: Doubles all mill you deal to opponents. Turns Traumatize into a full library and is the single biggest payoff in the archetype.

tz_key_commanders.name: Phenax, God of Deception
tz_key_commanders.why: Tap any creature to mill for its toughness. Rewards big, defensive bodies that are good at surviving anyway.

tz_key_commanders.name: Szadek, Lord of Secrets
tz_key_commanders.why: Doubles his own mill total on each successful hit. A commander-damage clock and a mill clock in the same card.

tz_key_commanders.name: Mirko Vosk, Mind Drinker
tz_key_commanders.why: Mills to four lands on connect, which in a typical Commander deck means far more than four cards.

tz_key_commanders.name: Anowon, the Ruin Thief
tz_key_commanders.why: Rogues mill on damage and grow as opponents' graveyards fill. The tribal-mill hybrid, and the most consistent build in the archetype.

tz_key_commanders.name: Circu, Dimir Lobotomist
tz_key_commanders.why: Exiles what it mills, which pre-empts every graveyard-recursion deck the mill plan would otherwise be feeding.

tz_key_commanders.name: Umbris, Fear Manifest
tz_key_commanders.why: Exiles cards from libraries and grows enormous doing it, converting the mill plan into commander damage as a backup.

tz_key_commanders.name: Lord Xander, the Collector
tz_key_commanders.why: Discard, mill, and sacrifice triggers stacked on one body. Slow but attacks every resource at once.

tz_key_commanders.name: Oona, Queen of the Fae
tz_key_commanders.why: Exiles from a library and makes a flier for each card of the chosen color, a mill effect that builds a board.

tz_key_commanders.name: Tasha, the Witch Queen
tz_key_commanders.why: Lets you cast what you mill from opponents, turning three libraries into your own card pool.

mill.tz_watch_out: Mill is the archetype most likely to make a table turn on you, because milling everyone reads as attacking everyone. It also actively helps graveyard decks: filling a Muldrotha player's yard is doing their work for them. Talk about it in your Rule 0 conversation, and know which pods it is a good fit for before you sit down.

spellslinger.plan: many cheap instants and sorceries each turn feed per-cast payoffs
stages: fill the deck with cheap, flexible spells
convert each cast to damage, tokens, cards or mana
hold interaction that also advances the engine
close with triggers, a token force or a large spell
wins: copied finisher or large X spell
spellslinger.weak: fragile payoff creatures; taxes (Eidolon of Rhetoric, Damping Sphere, Rule of Law); discard; slow board impact

src.sw: explosive chain turns; weak to taxes
src.cf: subs: cantrips, copy spells, big spells, magecraft; Demanding

tz_key_cards.name: Archmage Emeritus
tz_key_cards.why: Magecraft draw. Every instant and sorcery replaces itself, which is the single cleanest way to keep a chain from running out of gas.

tz_key_cards.name: Storm-Kiln Artist
tz_key_cards.why: A Treasure per spell, so the deck's own spell count pays for the rest of the turn. The most common enabler of a genuinely explosive turn.

tz_key_cards.name: Young Pyromancer
tz_key_cards.why: A 1/1 per spell for two mana. Converts a deck full of cheap cantrips into an actual board without changing the curve.

tz_key_cards.name: Thousand-Year Storm
tz_key_cards.why: Each spell copies itself once per spell already cast this turn. Expensive, but it turns the third spell of a turn into a game-ending one.

tz_key_cards.name: Jeska's Will
tz_key_cards.why: Mana and cards in one card, and with your commander out it delivers both. The premier red ritual in the archetype.

tz_key_cards.name: Underworld Breach
tz_key_cards.why: Escape lets you recast the instants and sorceries already in your graveyard, which is where a Spellslinger deck keeps most of its deck by turn six.

tz_key_cards.name: Past in Flames
tz_key_cards.why: Flashback on your whole graveyard for one turn. The classic way to make a second pass through everything you already cast.

tz_key_cards.name: Murmuring Mystic
tz_key_cards.why: A 1/3 that makes a flying blocker per instant or sorcery. Solves the archetype's real weakness: having no bodies while durdling.

tz_key_cards.name: Ral, Storm Conduit
tz_key_cards.why: Pings on every spell and copies your instants and sorceries. Doubles as a combo piece with any spell that copies itself.

tz_key_cards.name: Mizzix's Mastery
tz_key_cards.why: Recast the biggest sorcery in your graveyard; overloaded, recast all of them. A one-card turn that ends games out of nowhere.

tz_key_commanders.name: Veyran, Voice of Duality
tz_key_commanders.why: Doubles your own magecraft and cast triggers, so every payoff on the board pays twice.

tz_key_commanders.name: Zaffai, Thunder Conductor
tz_key_commanders.why: Scales with mana value rather than spell count, rewarding a deck that casts a few big spells instead of many small ones.

tz_key_commanders.name: Mizzix of the Izmagnus
tz_key_commanders.why: Experience counters make your instants and sorceries progressively cheaper, and the original cost-reduction commander.

tz_key_commanders.name: Niv-Mizzet, Parun
tz_key_commanders.why: Draw a card, deal a damage; deal damage, draw a card. A commander that is also the deck's win condition.

tz_key_commanders.name: Kess, Dissident Mage
tz_key_commanders.why: One free flashback per turn from the graveyard, which is why Grixis Spellslinger exists as its own lane.

tz_key_commanders.name: Talrand, Sky Summoner
tz_key_commanders.why: A 2/2 flier per instant or sorcery, mono-blue. The budget entry point to the archetype and still a real clock.

tz_key_commanders.name: Kalamax, the Stormsire
tz_key_commanders.why: Copies the first instant you cast each turn while tapped, pushing the deck toward instant speed and combat tricks.

tz_key_commanders.name: Balmor, Battlemage Captain
tz_key_commanders.why: Pumps and grants flying to the team per spell, turning a token board into lethal in one cantrip-heavy turn.

tz_key_commanders.name: Lier, Disciple of the Drowned
tz_key_commanders.why: Gives everything in your graveyard flashback and turns off counterspells, which is both an engine and a shield.

tz_key_commanders.name: Elsha of the Infinite
tz_key_commanders.why: Play off the top of your library at instant speed. Rewards a deck built almost entirely of cheap noncreature spells.

spellslinger.tz_watch_out: Spellslinger's failure mode is casting a lot of spells that do not add up to anything. A deck of cantrips with no payoff on the battlefield is a deck that drew cards and passed the turn. Keep enough payoff permanents that any given turn has something to trigger, and enough interaction that you are not simply durdling while three other players develop.

storm.plan: bank many cheap spells in one turn until the storm count is lethal
stages: cost reducers and rituals turn spells into mana and cards
commit to a payoff only with count and protection ready
storm.weak: one counterspell on the payoff; Rule of Law, Thalia taxes, graveyard hate; visible sculpting; long turns unwelcome in casual pods

stages: early: ramp, draw and tutor toward pieces
win in one moment, not through combat
combo.weak: single counterspell or removal; tutor punishers (Opposition Agent, Aven Mindcensor, Archivist of Oghma); hand attack; Null Rod, Collector Ouphe; stax strands tutors

src.tz: often a backup plan in other archetypes

tz_key_cards.name: Demonic Tutor
tz_key_cards.why: Two mana, any card, straight to hand. The cleanest tutor ever printed and the backbone of consistency.

tz_key_cards.name: Vampiric Tutor
tz_key_cards.why: One mana at instant speed for a card on top. Slower to use but cheap enough to hold up alongside protection.

tz_key_cards.name: Enlightened Tutor
tz_key_cards.why: Finds artifacts and enchantments at instant speed, which covers a large share of the format's combo pieces.

tz_key_cards.name: Thassa's Oracle
tz_key_cards.why: Win the game on its enter trigger with an empty library. The most-played alternate win condition in Commander.

tz_key_cards.name: Demonic Consultation
tz_key_cards.why: Exiles your whole library for one card, which is a drawback everywhere except next to Thassa's Oracle, where it is the combo.

tz_key_cards.name: Isochron Scepter
tz_key_cards.why: Imprints a cheap instant and recasts it every turn. Half of the format's most famous mana-generating loop.

tz_key_cards.name: Dramatic Reversal
tz_key_cards.why: Untaps all your nonland permanents. The other half: with enough mana rocks the loop generates infinite mana.

tz_key_cards.name: Kiki-Jiki, Mirror Breaker
tz_key_cards.why: Copies a creature with haste each turn, which is a two-card infinite with any creature that untaps or blinks him.

tz_key_cards.name: Protean Hulk
tz_key_cards.why: Fetches six mana value of creatures when it dies, so a single sacrifice assembles a whole combo from the library.

tz_key_cards.name: Ad Nauseam
tz_key_cards.why: Draws most of your deck at the cost of life. In a low-curve list it finds every piece at once.

tz_key_commanders.name: Kinnan, Bonder Prodigy
tz_key_commanders.why: Doubles mana from nonland sources and cheats big creatures out. One of the strongest mana engines in the format.

tz_key_commanders.name: Godo, Bandit Warlord
tz_key_commanders.why: Tutors Helm of the Host on entry, which grants infinite combat steps. A mono-red one-card combo.

tz_key_commanders.name: Thrasios, Triton Hero
tz_key_commanders.why: Converts infinite mana into drawing your library. The default outlet in cEDH, and legal as a solo commander.

tz_key_commanders.name: Captain Sisay
tz_key_commanders.why: Tutors any legendary permanent every turn, chaining into a pile of legends that lock or win.

tz_key_commanders.name: Winota, Joiner of Forces
tz_key_commanders.why: Puts Humans onto the battlefield from the library on attack. Snowballs into a game-ending turn immediately.

tz_key_commanders.name: Yisan, the Wanderer Bard
tz_key_commanders.why: Tutors creatures by escalating mana value, assembling a creature combo one verse counter at a time.

tz_key_commanders.name: Selvala, Heart of the Wilds
tz_key_commanders.why: Enormous mana from a single tap, which turns any big-mana payoff into a kill.

tz_key_commanders.name: Tivit, Seller of Secrets
tz_key_commanders.why: Makes Clue and Treasure tokens through voting, and combos cleanly with untap effects.

tz_key_commanders.name: Oswald Fiddlebender
tz_key_commanders.why: Sacrifices an artifact to tutor another onto the battlefield, chaining a combo out of the library for one mana a time.

tz_key_commanders.name: Krark, the Thumbless
tz_key_commanders.why: Coin-flip spell recursion that goes infinite with the right pairing. The most chaotic combo commander in common play.

combo.tz_watch_out: Combo is the archetype where power level is least visible from the outside, and where a mismatch is felt most sharply. A deck that wins on turn four in a pod expecting turn ten is not a better deck, it is a different game. Be specific in the Rule 0 conversation, saying that you have infinite combos and roughly when they land, and know which bracket your build belongs in.

counters.plan: grow creatures with +1/+1 counters and multiply them until the weakest creature is huge
stages: cast creatures that enter with counters
multipliers so each trigger gives more
protect the engine, attack with creatures that outgrow blocks
counters.weak: board wipes (Farewell, Toxic Deluge); Solemnity; Vampire Hexmage; setup turns; removal on doublers

tz_key_cards.name: Hardened Scales
tz_key_cards.why: One extra counter every time counters are placed. A one-drop that quietly doubles the deck's output all game.

tz_key_cards.name: Branching Evolution
tz_key_cards.why: Doubles counters placed on your creatures. The cleanest and most reliable multiplier in the archetype.

tz_key_cards.name: Corpsejack Menace
tz_key_cards.why: The same effect on a 4/4 body, so it doubles counters and pressures the board at the same time.

tz_key_cards.name: The Ozolith
tz_key_cards.why: Collects counters from creatures that die and moves them to a new creature. Makes removal cost you a body, not your investment.

tz_key_cards.name: Kalonian Hydra
tz_key_cards.why: Doubles the counters on every creature you control on attack. Two attacks usually ends the game.

tz_key_cards.name: Evolution Sage
tz_key_cards.why: Proliferates on every land drop, adding counters to every creature and planeswalker for free, every turn.

tz_key_cards.name: Master Biomancer
tz_key_cards.why: Every creature you play enters with counters equal to its power and becomes a Mutant. Scales the whole deck at once.

tz_key_cards.name: Conclave Mentor
tz_key_cards.why: An extra counter on placement plus lifegain when it dies. Cheap redundancy for the Hardened Scales effect.

tz_key_cards.name: Inspiring Call
tz_key_cards.why: Draws for every creature with a counter and makes them indestructible. Card advantage and a wrath answer in one instant.

tz_key_cards.name: Simic Ascendancy
tz_key_cards.why: Tracks growth counters and wins outright at twenty. An alternate win condition that costs the deck nothing to include.

tz_key_commanders.name: Ezuri, Claw of Progress
tz_key_commanders.why: Experience counters that pump a creature every turn, growing permanently across the game.

tz_key_commanders.name: Animar, Soul of Elements
tz_key_commanders.why: Grows on every creature cast and reduces their cost, so the deck accelerates as it gets bigger.

tz_key_commanders.name: Vorel of the Hull Clade
tz_key_commanders.why: Doubles counters on a permanent every turn, including artifacts and lands with counters on them.

tz_key_commanders.name: Hamza, Guardian of Arashin
tz_key_commanders.why: Creatures cost one less per creature with a counter, which makes a developed board fuel enormous turns.

tz_key_commanders.name: Kathril, Aspect Warper
tz_key_commanders.why: Distributes counters based on keywords in your graveyard, tying counters to a self-mill plan.

tz_key_commanders.name: Anafenza, the Foremost
tz_key_commanders.why: Counters on attack plus graveyard hate stapled on, which shuts down the recursion decks that beat you.

tz_key_commanders.name: Shalai and Hallar
tz_key_commanders.why: Turns counter placement into direct damage to every opponent, so growth is also a clock.

tz_key_commanders.name: Renata, Called to the Hunt
tz_key_commanders.why: Every creature enters with an extra counter. Mono-green, cheap, and it works with everything.

tz_key_commanders.name: Roalesk, Apex Hybrid
tz_key_commanders.why: Arrives with counters and proliferates twice when it dies, so removal still advances your board.

tz_key_commanders.name: Hapatra, Vizier of Poisons
tz_key_commanders.why: The minus-one-minus-one side: she turns counters into Snake tokens and doubles as repeatable removal.

counters.tz_watch_out: The doublers are the deck and they are all noncreature permanents, so a Vandalblast or a Back to Nature hurts more than a board wipe does. Spread the effect across creatures and enchantments rather than relying on one, and remember that counters do not survive a creature dying unless you have The Ozolith or similar. The archetype looks resilient but is only as durable as the bodies carrying it.

infect.plan: poison (infect/toxic) instead of life loss; 10 counters via a pumped evasive attacker plus proliferate
stages: pump an evasive attacker for 10 in one or two hits
infect.weak: table aggression; fog, deathtouch blockers, wipes; some pods ban poison; lifegain irrelevant to the clock

stages: gain life in repeat small increments
payoffs turn each trigger into value
use the life buffer to play patiently
close with drain loop, oversized board or Reservoir

cards: Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose

tz_key_cards.name: Exquisite Blood
tz_key_cards.why: Gain life whenever an opponent loses it. Half of the format's best-known two-card infinite combo.

tz_key_cards.name: Sanguine Bond
tz_key_cards.why: The other half: opponents lose life whenever you gain it. Together they loop until the table is at zero.

tz_key_cards.name: Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose
tz_key_cards.why: A cheaper Sanguine Bond on a creature, which makes the combo far easier to assemble and tutor for.

tz_key_cards.name: Aetherflux Reservoir
tz_key_cards.why: Gains escalating life per spell and pays fifty life to deal fifty damage. A win condition that needs no combat.

tz_key_cards.name: Archangel of Thune
tz_key_cards.why: Puts a counter on every creature you control whenever you gain life, converting incidental gain into a lethal board.

tz_key_cards.name: Well of Lost Dreams
tz_key_cards.why: Draw cards for life gained, up to the amount you paid. Turns the archetype's dead resource into cards.

tz_key_cards.name: Serra Ascendant
tz_key_cards.why: A one-drop 6/6 flying lifelink at thirty or more life, which in a forty-life format is almost immediately.

tz_key_cards.name: Soul Warden
tz_key_cards.why: A life for every creature entering, from anyone. Cheap, relentless, and the trigger most payoffs are counting.

tz_key_cards.name: Rhox Faithmender
tz_key_cards.why: Doubles all life you gain, which doubles every drain, draw, and counter your payoffs produce.

tz_key_cards.name: Felidar Sovereign
tz_key_cards.why: Wins the game outright at forty or more life on your upkeep. The most direct payoff the archetype has.

tz_key_commanders.name: Oloro, Ageless Ascetic
tz_key_commanders.why: Gains two life every upkeep even from the command zone, which makes him the format's most passive engine.

tz_key_commanders.name: Karlov of the Ghost Council
tz_key_commanders.why: Two counters per lifegain trigger and exiles creatures by spending them. Grows absurdly fast.

tz_key_commanders.name: Ayli, Eternal Pilgrim
tz_key_commanders.why: Sacrifices creatures for life, then exiles any permanent once you are ten life ahead. Lifegain as removal.

tz_key_commanders.name: Licia, Sanguine Tribune
tz_key_commanders.why: Costs less the more life you have gained and converts a chunk of your total into permanent power.

tz_key_commanders.name: Willowdusk, Essence Seer
tz_key_commanders.why: Moves life gained onto a creature as counters, or turns it into damage. The green-black bridge to counters.

tz_key_commanders.name: Trelasarra, Moon Dancer
tz_key_commanders.why: Scry and a counter on every lifegain trigger, on a two-drop. Cheap, fast, and consistent.

tz_key_commanders.name: Lathiel, the Bounteous Dawn
tz_key_commanders.why: Distributes counters equal to the life gained that turn across your creatures at end step.

tz_key_commanders.name: Liesa, Shroud of Dusk
tz_key_commanders.why: Drains every opponent whenever a creature dies and taxes their spells with life. Two payoffs on one body.

tz_key_commanders.name: Obzedat, Ghost Council
tz_key_commanders.why: Drains two every turn and exiles himself to dodge removal, returning to drain again.

tz_key_commanders.name: Heliod, Sun-Crowned
tz_key_commanders.why: Counters on lifegain and grants lifelink, which makes him both an engine and half of a famous combo.

lifegain.tz_watch_out: A high life total is not a win, and it can be an active liability: being at eighty makes you look untouchable, and tables respond by attacking the person they cannot ignore. Make sure the deck converts life into damage, cards, or counters rather than just accumulating it. Watch out too for how quickly the Exquisite Blood combo ends a game; if your pod is not expecting an infinite, say so before you sit down.

reuse with flicker spells and repeatable engines
finish with token engine or trigger loop

tz_key_cards.name: Ephemerate
tz_key_cards.why: One mana to blink a creature, with rebound so it does it again next turn. Two triggers and a removal dodge for a single card.

tz_key_cards.name: Eldrazi Displacer
tz_key_cards.why: A repeatable blink for three mana, usable at instant speed on any creature, including an opponent's, as removal.

tz_key_cards.name: Conjurer's Closet
tz_key_cards.why: Blinks a creature at the end of every one of your turns, for free, forever. The most reliable engine piece in the archetype.

tz_key_cards.name: Deadeye Navigator
tz_key_cards.why: Soulbond gives unlimited blinks for two mana each. Powerful enough to be a combo piece with half the format.

tz_key_cards.name: Ghostly Flicker
tz_key_cards.why: Blinks two permanents including lands and artifacts, which is what turns blink into an infinite-mana engine.

tz_key_cards.name: Displacer Kitten
tz_key_cards.why: Blinks a nonland permanent whenever you cast a noncreature spell. Ties the archetype to spellslinger and to combo.

tz_key_cards.name: Restoration Angel
tz_key_cards.why: A flash 3/4 flier that blinks a creature on entry. Value, a combat trick, and a removal dodge on one body.

tz_key_cards.name: Panharmonicon
tz_key_cards.why: Doubles enter triggers for creatures and artifacts, so every blink pays twice for no extra mana.

tz_key_cards.name: Solemn Simulacrum
tz_key_cards.why: Fetches a land on entry and draws on death. The archetype's benchmark for what a blink target should do.

tz_key_cards.name: Cloudshift
tz_key_cards.why: The one-mana baseline. Cheap, instant-speed, and often the difference between losing a creature and getting a free trigger.

tz_key_commanders.name: Brago, King Eternal
tz_key_commanders.why: Blinks all your nonland permanents on combat damage. The archetype's flagship and a notorious combo engine.

tz_key_commanders.name: Roon of the Hidden Realm
tz_key_commanders.why: A repeatable blink from the command zone every turn, in the three colors with the best targets.

tz_key_commanders.name: Yarok, the Desecrated
tz_key_commanders.why: Doubles every enter trigger you control, which turns each blink into two payoffs.

tz_key_commanders.name: Emiel the Blessed
tz_key_commanders.why: A three-mana repeatable blink outlet with no color requirements beyond green, and a combo engine besides.

tz_key_commanders.name: Chulane, Teller of Tales
tz_key_commanders.why: A card and a land on every creature cast, plus a bounce to reuse triggers. Value on every axis at once.

tz_key_commanders.name: Aminatou, the Fateshifter
tz_key_commanders.why: A planeswalker commander whose minus-one blinks a permanent every single turn, for free.

tz_key_commanders.name: Ranar the Ever-Watchful
tz_key_commanders.why: Makes a Spirit whenever you exile a card from hand or blink a permanent, so the engine builds a board.

tz_key_commanders.name: Ephara, God of the Polis
tz_key_commanders.why: Draws on every creature entering on any turn, which rewards flash and end-step blinking.

tz_key_commanders.name: Yorion, Sky Nomad
tz_key_commanders.why: Blinks any number of your permanents on entry, and can be recast repeatedly from the command zone.

tz_key_commanders.name: Thassa, Deep-Dwelling
tz_key_commanders.why: Blinks a creature at every end step and is an indestructible non-creature most of the time. Nearly impossible to answer.

blink.tz_watch_out: Blink decks are slow to threaten anything, and a pile of value creatures with no finisher can grind for an hour without winning. Make sure something in the deck converts the accumulated advantage into a victory. The archetype also relies on triggers, which means Torpor Orb and its family shut it off entirely, so keep an answer or two for artifacts and enchantments.

tz_key_cards.name: Smokestack

tz_key_cards.name: Tangle Wire

tz_key_cards.name: Sphere of Resistance

tz_key_cards.name: Thalia, Guardian of Thraben
tz_key_cards.why: The same tax on noncreature spells only, on a first-strike body that can pressure a player while it taxes.

tz_key_cards.name: Blood Moon

tz_key_cards.name: Cursed Totem
tz_key_cards.why: Turns off every creature's activated abilities, which is a one-card answer to mana dorks, sacrifice outlets, and most creature combos.

tz_key_cards.name: Ensnaring Bridge
tz_key_cards.why: Creatures with power greater than your hand size cannot attack. A stax deck empties its hand anyway, so this is close to one-sided.

tz_key_commanders.name: Grand Arbiter Augustin IV
tz_key_commanders.why: Your spells cost less and everyone else's cost more. Taxation from the command zone, on turn four, every game.

tz_key_commanders.name: Derevi, Empyrial Tactician
tz_key_commanders.why: Repeatedly taps and untaps permanents and returns from the command zone cheaply, which makes her nearly impossible to remove permanently.

tz_key_commanders.name: Lavinia, Azorius Renegade
tz_key_commanders.why: Counters any spell cast with more mana value than the caster's lands. Devastating against ritual-fuelled and free-spell decks.

tz_key_commanders.name: Tergrid, God of Fright
tz_key_commanders.why: Everything opponents sacrifice or discard comes to you instead. Turns denial into your own board.

tz_key_commanders.name: Braids, Cabal Minion
tz_key_commanders.why: Forces a sacrifice from every opponent every turn. Old, brutally simple, and banned in some circles for good reason.

tz_key_commanders.name: Hokori, Dust Drinker
tz_key_commanders.why: A Winter Orb on a body, in the command zone, available every game.

tz_key_commanders.name: Sen Triplets
tz_key_commanders.why: Locks a player out of casting and lets you play their hand. Denial and theft on the same trigger.

tz_key_commanders.name: Elesh Norn, Mother of Machines
tz_key_commanders.why: Doubles your enter-the-battlefield triggers and turns off everyone else's. A lock piece that also builds your engine.

tz_key_commanders.name: Queen Marchesa
tz_key_commanders.why: The monarch as a political lock: she creates a resource the table has to attack you for, while you defend it.

tz_key_commanders.name: Vorinclex, Voice of Hunger
tz_key_commanders.why: Your lands make double mana and opponents' lands enter tapped. Green's version of resource denial, and one of the most punishing.

stax.tz_watch_out: This is the archetype most likely to cause a genuinely bad evening. Stax makes other people's games less fun in a direct, visible way, and in a casual pod it often produces long turns where three players do nothing. That does not make it wrong to play. It makes it something to raise before the game starts. Check the bracket your pod is at, say what your deck does in the Rule 0 conversation, and be ready to sleeve up something else.

control.plan: decide which threats matter, answer them, win late with a protected finisher or engine
stages: hold mana and answer what matters
sweepers reset crowded boards then rebuild with draw
close with protected finisher or combo
control.weak: one-for-one answers lose value to three opponents; slow clocks; fast rebuilders

src.cf: subs: draw-go, tap-out control, pillowfort, mass removal

tz_key_cards.name: Counterspell
tz_key_cards.why: Two mana, no conditions. Still the baseline every other counterspell is measured against.

tz_key_cards.name: Cyclonic Rift
tz_key_cards.why: Overloaded, it returns every nonland permanent your opponents control at instant speed. The single most game-swinging card in the archetype.

tz_key_cards.name: Swords to Plowshares
tz_key_cards.why: One mana to exile any creature. The life gained is close to irrelevant at forty.

tz_key_cards.name: Wrath of God
tz_key_cards.why: Four mana, all creatures, no regeneration. Answering three players' boards with one card is how control keeps pace.

tz_key_cards.name: Toxic Deluge
tz_key_cards.why: A scaling sweeper paid for in life, which gets around indestructible and large creatures alike.

tz_key_cards.name: Rhystic Study
tz_key_cards.why: Taxes every spell the table casts, and either draws you cards or slows everyone down. Both outcomes are what control wants.

tz_key_cards.name: Mystic Remora
tz_key_cards.why: Draws enormously in the early turns for one mana, then retires. The best cheap draw engine in multiplayer.

tz_key_cards.name: Fierce Guardianship
tz_key_cards.why: A free counterspell with your commander out, which lets you tap out on your own turn and still hold up interaction.

tz_key_cards.name: Farewell
tz_key_cards.why: Modal exile of any combination of artifacts, creatures, enchantments, and graveyards. One card that answers whole strategies.

tz_key_cards.name: Nevinyrral's Disk
tz_key_cards.why: A repeatable-threat sweeper that hits artifacts and enchantments too, and is available in any color.

tz_key_commanders.name: Baral, Chief of Compliance
tz_key_commanders.why: Cheaper counterspells and loot on every counter. Mono-blue control with the draw problem partly solved.

tz_key_commanders.name: Teferi, Temporal Archmage
tz_key_commanders.why: A planeswalker commander that untaps four permanents each turn, so you counter on their turn and still develop on yours.

tz_key_commanders.name: Azor, the Lawbringer
tz_key_commanders.why: A sphinx that draws a large chunk of a deck and stops opponents casting instants and sorceries for a turn.

tz_key_commanders.name: Dragonlord Ojutai
tz_key_commanders.why: Hexproof while untapped and dig on damage. A control finisher that survives everything a control deck fears.

tz_key_commanders.name: Dragonlord Silumgar
tz_key_commanders.why: Steals a creature or planeswalker and keeps stealing as he is recast. Removal that becomes your threat.

tz_key_commanders.name: The Scarab God
tz_key_commanders.why: Scry and drain each upkeep, exiles graveyards for Zombies, and returns to hand instead of dying. Nearly unanswerable.

tz_key_commanders.name: Ertai Resurrected
tz_key_commanders.why: Flash plus a modal counter or removal on entry, and he returns to the command zone rather than dying.

tz_key_commanders.name: Rashmi, Eternities Crafter
tz_key_commanders.why: Free spells off the top on your first spell each turn, which fixes control's card-advantage math.

tz_key_commanders.name: Nymris, Oona's Trickster
tz_key_commanders.why: Draws whenever you cast on an opponent's turn, exactly the play pattern control already wants.

tz_key_commanders.name: Damia, Sage of Stone
tz_key_commanders.why: Refills you to seven cards every upkeep, which makes trading one-for-one with three opponents sustainable.

control.tz_watch_out: The archetype's real risk is being the table's police officer. If you counter everything, three players learn that you are the problem, and in a format where they can all attack you at once that is a losing position regardless of how good your answers are. Let some things resolve, save your counterspells for what actually beats you, and make sure the deck can close a game rather than only prolong it.

group_hug.plan: give the table cards, lands or mana and profit from how they use it
stages: steer attacks and removal toward others
pay off every draw or land drop
hold interaction for the best user of gifts
win with a hidden spell or late payoff
group_hug.weak: accelerates opponents; little pressure; hidden win conditions draw interaction

tz_key_cards.name: Howling Mine
tz_key_cards.why: An extra card for everyone each turn. The original group hug card, and still the cleanest statement of the plan.

tz_key_cards.name: Font of Mythos
tz_key_cards.why: Two extra cards for everyone. Doubles the effect and doubles the goodwill.

tz_key_cards.name: Rites of Flourishing
tz_key_cards.why: An extra card and an extra land drop for every player. Accelerates the whole table meaningfully, not just cosmetically.

tz_key_cards.name: Dictate of Kruphix
tz_key_cards.why: Flash makes it land at the end of the turn before yours, so you are the first to benefit from it.

tz_key_cards.name: Heartbeat of Spring
tz_key_cards.why: Lands produce double mana for everyone. Enormous, and it favours whoever has the best mana sink.

tz_key_cards.name: Horn of Greed
tz_key_cards.why: A card for every land drop by anyone. In a table with extra land drops going around this draws absurdly.

tz_key_cards.name: Kami of the Crescent Moon
tz_key_cards.why: A cheap, repeatable draw for everyone on a body, and a lightning rod that is not you.

tz_key_cards.name: Minds Aglow
tz_key_cards.why: A joined-forces draw where every player contributes mana. Generous, and it refills your hand for a fraction of the cost.

tz_key_cards.name: Collective Voyage
tz_key_cards.why: The land version of the same idea. Ramps the whole table, and you chose the timing.

tz_key_cards.name: Braids, Conjurer Adept
tz_key_cards.why: Everyone puts a permanent onto the battlefield from hand each turn. The most generous effect in the archetype and the most easily abused.

tz_key_commanders.name: Kynaios and Tiro of Meletis
tz_key_commanders.why: A card and a land for everyone each turn. The archetype's flagship, and four colors of tools to exploit it.

tz_key_commanders.name: Zedruu the Greathearted
tz_key_commanders.why: Gives away permanents and draws and gains life for each. Turns generosity into a genuine engine.

tz_key_commanders.name: Phelddagrif
tz_key_commanders.why: The original hug: every ability helps you and helps an opponent. Old, strange, and beloved.

tz_key_commanders.name: Kwain, Itinerant Meddler
tz_key_commanders.why: Each player may draw and gain life. Cheap, symmetrical, and a famous engine piece for decks that draw better than the table.

tz_key_commanders.name: Selvala, Explorer Returned
tz_key_commanders.why: Parley gives everyone cards and you the mana. Generous in appearance, lopsided in practice.

tz_key_commanders.name: Edric, Spymaster of Trest
tz_key_commanders.why: Everyone draws for connecting with a creature, which points the whole table away from you and at each other.

tz_key_commanders.name: Braids, Conjurer Adept
tz_key_commanders.why: Free permanents for all, every turn. You are the one who built a deck around abusing it.

tz_key_commanders.name: Kenrith, the Returned King
tz_key_commanders.why: Five abilities anyone can activate, in five colors. The most flexible political commander in the format.

tz_key_commanders.name: Xyris, the Writhing Storm
tz_key_commanders.why: Forces opponents to draw and rewards you with a Snake for each. The clearest hug-into-win pipeline.

tz_key_commanders.name: Nekusar, the Mindrazer
tz_key_commanders.why: The group-slug inversion: everyone draws extra and takes damage for it. The same cards, aimed the other way.

group_hug.tz_watch_out: Group hug earns a reputation quickly, and it is usually deserved. A table that has been handed forty cards over eight turns and then loses to a Psychosis Crawler will remember. Decide what your deck is, say so at the start, and if it is a hug-into-kill deck, tell people. The strategy is fine; the ambush is what causes friction. The other failure mode is the sincere one: a genuine hug deck can accelerate a stronger deck into winning far sooner than it would have.

enchantress.plan: cheap enchantments replace themselves through draw triggers; constellation or aura payoff converts them to a win
stages: finish with constellation, tokens or aura Voltron
enchantress.weak: enchantment removal and wipes (Farewell, Bane of Progress, Back to Nature); losing enchantresses; payoff-heavy hands

src.cf: subs: aura, enchantment tokens, constellation, pillowfort

tz_key_cards.name: Argothian Enchantress
tz_key_cards.why: A one-mana body with shroud that draws on every enchantment. The best draw engine in the archetype and the hardest to remove.

tz_key_cards.name: Enchantress's Presence
tz_key_cards.why: The same effect on an enchantment, which means it also triggers your other enchantresses when it resolves.

tz_key_cards.name: Eidolon of Blossoms
tz_key_cards.why: Constellation draw, so it triggers on enchantments entering rather than being cast, so it catches tokens and recursion too.

tz_key_cards.name: Setessan Champion
tz_key_cards.why: Draws and grows on each constellation trigger, turning the draw engine into a genuine threat.

tz_key_cards.name: Sigil of the Empty Throne
tz_key_cards.why: A 4/4 Angel for every enchantment cast. The most common way an enchantress deck actually ends a game.

tz_key_cards.name: Sphere of Safety
tz_key_cards.why: Attacking you costs mana per enchantment you control, which in this deck quickly means nobody can attack at all.

tz_key_cards.name: Starfield of Nyx
tz_key_cards.why: Returns an enchantment from your graveyard each upkeep and animates the whole board once you have five.

tz_key_cards.name: Sanctum Weaver
tz_key_cards.why: Taps for mana equal to your enchantment count. Ramp that scales with exactly the thing the deck is already doing.

tz_key_cards.name: Serra's Sanctum
tz_key_cards.why: A land that taps for white mana per enchantment. Expensive to acquire, but no other card matches its ceiling here.

tz_key_cards.name: Replenish
tz_key_cards.why: Returns every enchantment from your graveyard to the battlefield at once. The archetype's answer to a board wipe, and often a win on the spot.

tz_key_commanders.name: Sythis, Harvest's Hand
tz_key_commanders.why: Draws and gains life on every enchantment cast, from a two-mana command zone. The most efficient starting point in the archetype.

tz_key_commanders.name: Tuvasa the Sunlit
tz_key_commanders.why: Draws on your first enchantment each turn and grows with the count, doubling as a Voltron threat.

tz_key_commanders.name: Estrid, the Masked
tz_key_commanders.why: A planeswalker commander that untaps your enchanted permanents and recurs auras from the graveyard.

tz_key_commanders.name: Zur the Enchanter
tz_key_commanders.why: Tutors an enchantment directly onto the battlefield on every attack, which makes the deck brutally consistent.

tz_key_commanders.name: Daxos the Returned
tz_key_commanders.why: Builds experience counters on enchantment casts and spends them on scaling Spirit tokens.

tz_key_commanders.name: Calix, Destiny's Hand
tz_key_commanders.why: A planeswalker that finds enchantments, taps down threats, and returns auras. Removal and card advantage in one.

tz_key_commanders.name: Kestia, the Cultivator
tz_key_commanders.why: Bestow lets her dodge removal, and she draws for each enchanted creature attacking.

tz_key_commanders.name: Siona, Captain of the Pyleas
tz_key_commanders.why: A token per aura and a lethal combo with Shielded by Faith. The aggressive aura variant of the archetype.

tz_key_commanders.name: Sigarda, Host of Herons
tz_key_commanders.why: Hexproof and immunity to sacrifice effects, which protects a heavy aura investment from the things auras usually lose to.

tz_key_commanders.name: Gylwain, Casting Director
tz_key_commanders.why: Makes a free Role token on every creature you cast, so the enchantment count climbs without spending cards.

enchantress.tz_watch_out: Enchantress can draw twenty cards and still not win. The archetype's classic failure is assembling a beautiful, unattackable board with no way to close, while the table plays around it. Decide early how the deck wins (Angels, an aura-based commander kill, or a combo) and run enough copies of that plan that drawing half your library actually finds one.

artifacts.plan: connect cheap artifacts, rocks and utility pieces into one engine
stages: deploy cheap artifacts and rocks to critical mass
cost reducers/affinity/Treasure cast several per turn
win with constructs, loops, drain or one big artifact
artifacts.weak: mass artifact removal (Vandalblast, Farewell, Bane of Progress); Collector Ouphe, Stony Silence; slow start

src.cf: subs: artifact tokens, affinity, equipment, artifact combo

tz_key_cards.name: Urza's Saga
tz_key_cards.why: A land that makes a Construct scaling with your artifact count and then tutors a cheap artifact. Enormous value from a land slot.

tz_key_cards.name: Foundry Inspector
tz_key_cards.why: Artifacts cost one less. Cost reduction is what turns a hand of artifacts into a single explosive turn.

tz_key_cards.name: Cranial Plating
tz_key_cards.why: Plus one power per artifact you control, with a black-mana equip at instant speed. The archetype's classic one-hit kill.

tz_key_cards.name: Steel Overseer
tz_key_cards.why: A counter on every artifact creature each turn. Slow to start and unbeatable if ignored for three turns.

tz_key_cards.name: Goblin Welder
tz_key_cards.why: Swaps an artifact on the battlefield for one in a graveyard, free, every turn. Recursion and disruption at once.

tz_key_cards.name: Krark-Clan Ironworks
tz_key_cards.why: Sacrifice any artifact for two mana. The engine behind most artifact combo loops in the format.

tz_key_cards.name: Mystic Forge
tz_key_cards.why: Play artifacts off the top of your library. In a deck that is mostly artifacts, this is drawing several extra cards a turn.

tz_key_cards.name: Wurmcoil Engine
tz_key_cards.why: Six-mana lifelink and deathtouch that leaves two tokens behind. The fair, unglamorous card that stabilises boards.

tz_key_cards.name: Scrap Trawler
tz_key_cards.why: Returns a cheaper artifact whenever an artifact you control dies, chaining into itself across a sacrifice loop.

tz_key_cards.name: Unwinding Clock
tz_key_cards.why: Untaps all your artifacts on every player's turn, turning tap abilities into four activations per round instead of one.

tz_key_commanders.name: Urza, Lord High Artificer
tz_key_commanders.why: Taps artifacts for mana, makes a Construct on entry, and digs into your library. Arguably the strongest artifact commander printed.

tz_key_commanders.name: Breya, Etherium Shaper
tz_key_commanders.why: Four colors, a free Thopter pair, and three modal abilities. The most flexible artifact command zone in the format.

tz_key_commanders.name: Osgir, the Reconstructor
tz_key_commanders.why: Exiles artifacts from the graveyard to make two copies. Turns every dead artifact into two live ones.

tz_key_commanders.name: Emry, Lurker of the Loch
tz_key_commanders.why: Self-mills and casts artifacts out of the graveyard each turn, at a cost that drops as your artifact count rises.

tz_key_commanders.name: Sharuum the Hegemon
tz_key_commanders.why: Reanimates an artifact on entry, which with a clone effect is one of the oldest combos in Commander.

tz_key_commanders.name: Jhoira, Weatherlight Captain
tz_key_commanders.why: Draws a card for every historic spell you cast. Card advantage that scales directly with artifact count.

tz_key_commanders.name: Shorikai, Genesis Engine
tz_key_commanders.why: A vehicle commander that makes a Pilot and loots every turn without ever attacking.

tz_key_commanders.name: Daretti, Scrap Savant
tz_key_commanders.why: A planeswalker commander whose whole kit is discarding artifacts and returning them, with an emblem finisher.

tz_key_commanders.name: Arcum Dagsson
tz_key_commanders.why: Tutors any artifact from the library each turn by sacrificing an artifact creature. Ruthlessly consistent, and famously divisive.

tz_key_commanders.name: Karn, Silver Golem
tz_key_commanders.why: Animates your noncreature artifacts, and being genuinely colorless lets the deck run every colorless land and artifact in the format.

artifacts.tz_watch_out: Artifact removal is the most commonly played removal in Commander after creature removal, and mass artifact destruction hits this deck harder than a board wipe hits most. Green and red both have one-sided sweepers for artifacts specifically. Spread your value across enough permanents that no single Vandalblast is a concession, and keep some recursion so the sweeper is a setback rather than an ending.

superfriends.plan: planeswalker density protected by blockers; loyalty doubling and extra activations
stages: activate again; surviving walkers are a resource
multiple ultimates in one turn via doubling
superfriends.weak: walkers without defense are free attack targets; slow and mana-hungry; archenemy after two ultimates

src.tz: Atraxa, Carth the Lion, Sisay, Commodore Guff, Freyalise, Dihada, Nahiri, Jared Carthalion, Ramos, Saheeli commanders

tz_key_cards.name: Doubling Season
tz_key_cards.why: Planeswalkers enter with double loyalty, which means most of them can ultimate the turn they land.

tz_key_cards.name: The Chain Veil
tz_key_cards.why: Activate each planeswalker one additional time per turn. The archetype's signature engine, and its most abusable card.

tz_key_cards.name: Oath of Teferi
tz_key_cards.why: The same extra activation on an enchantment, plus a blink trigger on entry. Cheaper and harder to remove.

tz_key_cards.name: Deepglow Skate
tz_key_cards.why: Doubles the counters on any permanents you choose, usually every planeswalker at once, straight into multiple ultimates.

tz_key_cards.name: Vorinclex, Monstrous Raider
tz_key_cards.why: Doubles counters you place and halves everyone else's. A one-sided Doubling Season on a hasty body.

tz_key_cards.name: Ugin, the Spirit Dragon
tz_key_cards.why: A colorless sweeper that leaves your board intact, since almost everything in a superfriends deck is colorless or a planeswalker.

tz_key_cards.name: Elspeth, Sun's Champion
tz_key_cards.why: Makes three blockers a turn and wipes big creatures. Defends the whole team, which is the job that matters.

tz_key_cards.name: Interplanar Beacon
tz_key_cards.why: A land that fixes for planeswalkers, gains life when you cast one, and costs nothing to include.

tz_key_cards.name: Karn Liberated
tz_key_cards.why: Colorless, high loyalty, exiles any permanent, and fits into any deck in the archetype regardless of colors.

tz_key_cards.name: Nissa, Who Shakes the World
tz_key_cards.why: Doubles green mana from Forests and makes 3/3 lands that defend the rest of the team.

tz_key_commanders.name: Atraxa, Praetors' Voice
tz_key_commanders.why: Proliferate every end step, in the four colors with the best walkers. The definitive superfriends commander.

tz_key_commanders.name: Carth the Lion
tz_key_commanders.why: Planeswalkers enter with an extra counter and cost less to find. Quiet, cheap, and relentlessly consistent.

tz_key_commanders.name: Sisay, Weatherlight Captain
tz_key_commanders.why: Tutors any legendary permanent, including planeswalkers, and grows with each one on the battlefield.

tz_key_commanders.name: Dihada, Binder of Wills
tz_key_commanders.why: A planeswalker commander that draws, gains life, and protects legends. Mardu superfriends in one card.

tz_key_commanders.name: Commodore Guff
tz_key_commanders.why: Adds loyalty to a walker each turn and returns them from the graveyard. Built for this exact deck.

tz_key_commanders.name: Freyalise, Llanowar's Fury
tz_key_commanders.why: A planeswalker commander that makes Elves, so the team defends itself while the loyalty climbs.

tz_key_commanders.name: Nahiri, the Lithomancer
tz_key_commanders.why: Mono-white equipment-and-walkers, with a soldier token that keeps attackers busy.

tz_key_commanders.name: Jared Carthalion
tz_key_commanders.why: Grows with the monarch and can be a planeswalker magnet in a Naya shell that lacks blue's defensive tools.

tz_key_commanders.name: Ramos, Dragon Engine
tz_key_commanders.why: Stores counters from multicolor spells and dumps them into mana for a five-color walker suite.

tz_key_commanders.name: Saheeli, the Gifted
tz_key_commanders.why: A planeswalker commander whose Thopters defend the board while her ultimate copies artifacts for a win.

superfriends.tz_watch_out: A planeswalker with four loyalty in a four-player game is a planeswalker with one loyalty. The archetype fails when it plays walkers without defence: every one becomes a free attack target that dies before it does anything. Build the fort first: deterrent enchantments, blockers, and sweepers, then the walkers. Superfriends is also mana-hungry and slow, so expect to be the archdeck target once two ultimates have resolved.

burn.weak: single-target burn is inefficient in multiplayer; lifegain

turn 3-5: oversized threats that outclass blockers
anthems, haste and attack triggers scale the bodies
extra combats and combat draw refuel

extra combats for 40+ in a turn

tz_key_cards.name: Embercleave
tz_key_cards.why: Cost reduction on a wide board, then double strike and trample at instant speed. Converts a stalled attack into lethal after blockers.

tz_key_cards.name: Iroas, God of Victory
tz_key_cards.why: Your attackers cannot be blocked by more than one creature and do not take damage from blockers. Attacking becomes nearly free.

tz_key_cards.name: Anger
tz_key_cards.why: Grants haste to your whole team from the graveyard, permanently, as long as you control a Mountain.

tz_key_cards.name: Hammer of Purphoros
tz_key_cards.why: An anthem-plus-haste enchantment that also makes blockers, so the deck keeps pressuring without overextending.

tz_key_cards.name: Aggravated Assault
tz_key_cards.why: Repeatable extra combat steps. With any mana-positive attack trigger this becomes an outright kill.

tz_key_cards.name: Berserk
tz_key_cards.why: One mana to double a creature's power and give it trample. The classic surprise kill from a board that looked survivable.

tz_key_cards.name: Return of the Wildspeaker
tz_key_cards.why: Draws cards equal to your biggest creature's power, or pumps the team. Solves aggro's card-advantage problem in green.

tz_key_cards.name: Elesh Norn, Grand Cenobite
tz_key_cards.why: Plus-two-plus-two for you and minus-two-minus-two for everyone else. Frequently a one-sided board wipe and a lethal attack in one card.

tz_key_cards.name: Dolmen Gate
tz_key_cards.why: Your attacking creatures take no combat damage, which lets a smaller board attack into a bigger one every turn.

tz_key_cards.name: Ohran Frostfang
tz_key_cards.why: Deathtouch and a card for every attacker. Makes blocking suicidal and refills your hand while you swing.

tz_key_commanders.name: Isshin, Two Heavens as One
tz_key_commanders.why: Doubles every attack trigger in the deck. The most build-around aggressive commander of recent years.

tz_key_commanders.name: Xenagos, God of Revels
tz_key_commanders.why: Haste and doubled power to one creature each combat. Turns any large body into an immediate kill threat.

tz_key_commanders.name: Neheb, the Eternal
tz_key_commanders.why: Mana in your second main phase for damage dealt, so a big attack pays for the next threat.

tz_key_commanders.name: Aurelia, Exemplar of Justice
tz_key_commanders.why: Mentor plus escalating buffs, and she pushes damage through with trample and first strike as the counters pile up.

tz_key_commanders.name: Zurgo Helmsmasher
tz_key_commanders.why: A 7/2 haste for five that cannot be destroyed on your turn. Aggro reduced to its bluntest form.

tz_key_commanders.name: Gahiji, Honored One
tz_key_commanders.why: Pumps every attacker that is not attacking you, which turns the whole table into your offence.

tz_key_commanders.name: Wulfgar of Icewind Dale
tz_key_commanders.why: Doubles attack and haste triggers for your team, in a color pair full of them.

tz_key_commanders.name: Ilharg, the Raze-Boar
tz_key_commanders.why: Puts a creature from hand onto the battlefield attacking, then returns it. Cheats out giants every combat.

tz_key_commanders.name: Ruric Thar, the Unbowed
tz_key_commanders.why: A 6/6 vigilance that punishes noncreature spells, so the control decks pay for the turns they spend answering you.

tz_key_commanders.name: Toski, Bearer of Secrets
tz_key_commanders.why: Indestructible, must attack, and draws a card for every creature that connects. Aggro that never runs out of cards.

stompy.tz_watch_out: The politics are the hard part. Attacking early makes you the visible threat, and three opponents can agree to deal with you long before your deck is finished. Spread damage rather than focusing one player down unless you can finish them, and be realistic about the deck's clock. An aggro deck that has not won by turn eight is usually the worst deck at the table.

tz_key_cards.name: Crucible of Worlds
tz_key_cards.why: Play lands from your graveyard. The card that turns every fetchland and sacrifice land into a repeatable engine.

tz_key_cards.name: Ramunap Excavator
tz_key_cards.why: The same effect on a creature, which means green can tutor for it. Redundancy is what makes the engine reliable.

tz_key_cards.name: Life from the Loam
tz_key_cards.why: Dredge back three lands a turn. The most efficient land-recursion engine ever printed, and it never runs out.

tz_key_cards.name: Splendid Reclamation
tz_key_cards.why: Returns every land from your graveyard to the battlefield at once, triggering landfall for each of them.

tz_key_cards.name: Avenger of Zendikar
tz_key_cards.why: A Plant per land, then pumps them all on every landfall. The archetype's most reliable one-card win condition.

tz_key_cards.name: Field of the Dead
tz_key_cards.why: A 2/2 Zombie for every land drop once you have seven differently named lands. Free bodies from a land slot.

tz_key_cards.name: Exploration
tz_key_cards.why: An extra land drop every turn for one mana. Doubles the trigger count for the whole game.

tz_key_cards.name: Tireless Tracker
tz_key_cards.why: A Clue on every landfall and counters on itself when you crack them. Card advantage that also becomes a threat.

tz_key_cards.name: Aftermath Analyst
tz_key_cards.why: Self-mills, then returns every land from your graveyard when sacrificed. A modern Splendid Reclamation on a body.

tz_key_commanders.name: Lord Windgrace
tz_key_commanders.why: A planeswalker commander that recurs lands, draws, and makes 2/2 Cats. Purpose-built for the archetype.

tz_key_commanders.name: The Gitrog Monster
tz_key_commanders.why: Draws on every land put into the graveyard and eats a land each upkeep. Value engine and infamous combo piece.

tz_key_commanders.name: Titania, Protector of Argoth
tz_key_commanders.why: A 5/3 Elemental for every land that hits your graveyard. Converts a fetchland into an army.

tz_key_commanders.name: Tatyova, Benthic Druid
tz_key_commanders.why: A card and a life on every landfall. The friendliest entry point to the archetype and still one of the best.

tz_key_commanders.name: Omnath, Locus of Creation
tz_key_commanders.why: Escalating payouts on the first, second, and third landfall each turn. Rewards extra land drops directly.

tz_key_commanders.name: Aesi, Tyrant of Gyre Strait
tz_key_commanders.why: An extra land drop and a card on your first land each turn, Tatyova plus Exploration in the command zone.

tz_key_commanders.name: Multani, Yavimaya's Avatar
tz_key_commanders.why: Grows with lands on the battlefield and in the graveyard, and returns to hand from either. A recurring Voltron threat.

tz_key_commanders.name: Sasaya, Orochi Ascendant
tz_key_commanders.why: Flips once you hold seven lands and then makes each land tap for its whole type. Absurd mana from a mono-green shell.

tz_key_commanders.name: Ob Nixilis, the Fallen
tz_key_commanders.why: Landfall that drains three from an opponent and grows him by three. A mono-black clock built on land drops.

tz_key_commanders.name: Kodama of the East Tree
tz_key_commanders.why: Every permanent entering lets you put another from hand onto the battlefield, chaining off every land drop.

lands_matter.tz_watch_out: This is a slow archetype whose best turns come late, and it can spend the first six turns doing nothing that looks like a threat. That is usually fine (nobody attacks the lands player) but it means the deck needs a real payoff and enough draw to find it. Watch out too for combo lines the archetype falls into by accident: several lands commanders assemble loops that end games abruptly, which may be more than your pod signed up for.

outlaws.plan: typal ninja-pirate-rogue-assassin-mercenary-warlock deck that triggers on committing crimes (targeting opponents)
stages: mid: crime triggers (target an opponent, their spell or permanent) pay off
lords and tutors for the outlaw types
close with evasive outlaw swarm or a crime payoff
outlaws.weak: wipes; few payoffs outside outlaw types; targeted removal on lords; tribal filler dilutes the deck
outlaws.notes: Outlaws is a mechanic family (Thunder Junction), not a creature type; tag coverage is partial (types plus lords)

clones.plan: copy the best permanent on the table, yours or theirs, and recur copy effects
stages: play a flexible clone on turn 3-5
copy the strongest creature or ETB value piece
add copy triggers (Sakashima, Helm of the Host)
clones.weak: no good targets on an empty board; wipes; counterspells on key clones

extra_combats.plan: extra combat steps multiply attack triggers and damage per turn
extra_combats.weak: fog; blockers; wipes; one creature carries the combat
extra_combats.notes: no ftag marks extra-combat effects; trigger:beginning_of_combat is coarse (see note)

mutate.plan: stack mutate creatures onto the best body so every mutate trigger and attack trigger repeats
stages: early: cheap non-Human bodies as targets
mutate.weak: removal on a mutate stack loses cards; Human targets are illegal; wipes
mutate.notes: only 34 mutate cards in the pool

polymorph.plan: sacrifice a cheap creature to put a bigger one onto the battlefield from the library
stages: bomb has ETB or an immediate win
polymorph.weak: counterspells on the spell; no bomb in the library; edict removal
polymorph.notes: no polymorph ftag; signals are coarse

self_mill.plan: put cards from your own library into the graveyard, then use them with recursion and graveyard payoffs
self_mill.weak: graveyard hate; exile removal; self-mill risk in a tight library

energy.plan: generate energy counters and spend them on repeatable effects
stages: mid: spend energy on engines and attacks
energy.weak: wipes; the colours with energy cards are few; energy is not a payoff on its own
energy.notes: counter:energy matches 131 cards; producer and payoff share the tag (no split in the pool)

vehicles.plan: vehicles are the threats; crew creatures supply the pilot; vehicle payoffs reward the count
stages: deploy vehicles that outclass the crew cost
close with a big vehicle or crewed alpha
vehicles.weak: artifact removal; wipes leave vehicles but kill the crew; Torpor Orb
vehicles.notes: niche:vehicle only 13 cards; kw:crew is on the vehicles themselves (174 cards)

sagas.plan: sagas deliver chapter value over turns; recursion, proliferation and lore-counter tricks reuse them
stages: reuse chapters with lore-counter effects and blink
recur sagas with sacrifice or flicker
close with the last chapter payoffs
sagas.weak: enchantment removal; sagas are slow; low stand-alone power

discard.plan: make opponents discard, then punish an empty hand or a cluttered graveyard
stages: early: cheap discard to strip hands
close with a drain payoff or a locked table
discard.weak: three opponents refill; discard is weak against topdecks; speed

group_slug.plan: symmetrical or each-player damage and life loss that favour a deck prepared for it
stages: close with the last life total
group_slug.weak: lifegain; fog; faster decks; politics (you are the obvious threat)

forced_combat.plan: force opposing creatures to attack each other or you, and win by choosing the fights
stages: goad/must-attack effects aim the table at each other
wins: opponents fight each other, you finish
forced_combat.weak: fog; opponents with no creatures; aggro decks you cannot block
forced_combat.notes: goad is an oracle-text tag (deckgen/text_tags.py, 81 cards); must_attack covers 88 cards

pillow_fort.plan: attack taxes and deterrents keep attackers away while a late engine wins
stages: mid: card advantage and a defended engine
pillow_fort.weak: commander damage from decks that ignore the tax; enchantment removal; no pressure on others

upkeep_triggers.plan: turn-start payoffs: upkeep triggers that grow or cost, doubled by trigger copiers
wins: engine pile that outgrows the table
upkeep_triggers.weak: enchantment/artifact removal; slow; upkeep triggers also appear on cards unrelated to the plan
upkeep_triggers.notes: trigger:upkeep matches 711 cards; filter in the builder needs the commander

treasure.plan: make Treasure and convert it to mana, drain or sacrifice value

theft.plan: take opponents' permanents or cast their cards, then profit from the borrowed pieces
stages: steal the best permanent or spell
sacrifice or flicker stolen permanents for value
win with the table's own cards
theft.weak: removal on the stolen card; slow without a steal target
